title: Nuclear-cleanup remedies can prefigure future land use while transfer, reuse, and recontamination remain open
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-27-108063 review of future land use planning at selected Department of Energy nuclear-cleanup sites
geography: United States Department of Energy cleanup sites and surrounding local communities, regulators, tribes, and future land users

observations.period: Selected DOE cleanup sites and October 16, 2026 GAO report

denominator.unit: DOE cleanup sites selected by GAO for review across regulatory frameworks, cleanup stages, and future land uses

future_land_use_plans.value: DOE created initial future-land-use plans with local-community coordination as early as 1992 at all six selected sites; plans inform but do not bind cleanup assumptions
future_land_use_plans.unit: reported planning condition across selected sites

cleanup_use_alignment.value: Oak Ridge, Paducah, Portsmouth, and Savannah River cleanup levels aligned with industrial-use plans; nearly a third of Hanford and most contaminated Idaho areas received standards more stringent than anticipated conservation, preservation, or industrial uses

industrial_reuse.unit: selected sites where DOE transferred or leased a small amount of land to communities or private entities for industrial use

cleanup_cost_horizon.value: $641 billion to $840 billion estimated for cleaning up 15 remaining sites, with completion estimated in 2100
cleanup_cost_horizon.unit: reported national DOE cleanup estimate and horizon

reuse_tradeoffs.value: stakeholders cited possible economic growth, high-quality jobs, and local tax revenue alongside risks of diverting cleanup resources, pollution or recontamination, and future DOE liabilities; new initiatives include energy development, nuclear-fuel-cycle hubs, and co-located AI data centers

land_use_conversion.unit: parcel-level transfer, occupancy, employment, tax receipt, exposure, recontamination, liability, community consent, or long-term health outcome

observations.method: Structured extraction from GAO-27-108063, based on laws, regulations, policies, agency documents, site review at six selected DOE cleanup sites, two site visits, and interviews with DOE officials, regulators, tribal officials, and community stakeholders. Future-land-use plans, cleanup standards, transfers, tradeoffs, program scale, and post-transfer outcomes are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The six sites were selected to represent different frameworks, cleanup stages, and future land uses and are not a census of DOE sites. A cleanup standard aligned with a future-use assumption does not itself establish actual exposure or safety performance. The report does not provide a common parcel-level series for transfer, occupancy, jobs, tax revenue, recontamination, consent, or health outcomes.
observations.subgroup: Communities, tribes, regulators, workers, future residents, industrial users, private entities, and local governments near DOE nuclear-cleanup sites, with different exposure, economic, and decision-making positions.
observations.counterinterpretation: More stringent cleanup can preserve options or reflect precaution rather than waste, while industrial reuse can bring jobs and tax base; conversely, a nonbinding land-use assumption and later transfer can create durable exposure or liability risks if future uses exceed the remedy's contemplated conditions.

related_sources.claim: The official accessible report contains the selected-site future-land-use, cleanup-standard, transfer, and stakeholder-tradeoff findings.
GAO identifies a related defense-nuclear-waste report with recommendations concerning future-land-use authority and multi-use cleanup cost and schedule analysis.

boundary: This record advances a bounded cleanup-remedy-to-future-land-use and industrial-reuse route. It does not establish parcel-level transfer or occupancy, exposure, recontamination, jobs, tax receipts, community consent, health outcomes, liability realization, or national DOE cleanup performance.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Canonical GAO product URL string used as a stable source identifier; accessible report and related report links are retained for reproduction.
